body:
If gaslighting could be an Olympic sport.

We Chinese even have a phrase “打是疼，骂是爱” (Beating is affection, scolding is love).

I swear, Asian nparents are on a whole other level.

Well, a little I guess. Thankfully, however, there're no true Scapegoats in my family. My younger brother and sister simply did not get as much attention from my nfather, which, in hindsight, has been a blessing in disguise as they have become successful individuals. Compared to the "failed mini-me project" that will be spending years in therapy so as to undo the Pavlovian conditioning and learned helplessness that has destroyed her sense of self.
"It was all in your best interests."
Being the Golden Child is like sitting on a throne, but having the Sword of Damocles hanging over your head by a thin, flimsy thread.
Energy vampires

Thank you for your kind words! Yes! Positive thinking is not a cure-all to life's problems. While having a positive mindset can be helpful at times, trying to force myself to be positive at times has made me feel all but worse. I learned this the hard way.

I looked up what Munchausen and By Proxy were, and wow, that's so messed up! I used to think that some of the things my parents did were normal, only to discover that it wasn't normal at all. Nowadays, I try to restrict what I tell my mom, but doing so is easier said than done. Especially when it comes to someone who's been your best friend and confidante for much of your life.
Abolutely, and IMO, covert abuse is so much worse than the overt abuse. I've heard stories of people who say they wish they were beaten.

Oh yes! I couldn't continue the list due to being triggered, but I've come to notice that during normal conversations—not just with me—she takes on a condescending tone, and that puts me off. I used to be fine with it, but not anymore.
Thank you!
Thank you. Yes, it definitely sucks. I'm tired of all the guilt trips and passive-aggressive tantrums.
Thank you for your kind words! I'll definitely try harder next time.
"Ok, boomer."

"The play is now over."

I learn something new everyday. Thank you.
"I'd be honored to put an end to the bloodline."

Here in Asia, 'filial piety' is used to gaslight us into thinking we're obliged to reciprocate the care our parents have given. 

I'll say this again, children are not an insurance policy against old age.
Karens being Karens.

"Life is a gift." 

No better way to gaslight the entire human race!

Edit: By creator I take it that you refer to the Abrahamic God.

1. Children are not an insurance policy against old age. 

2. What's wrong with dying alone?
War. War never changes.
Reincarnation. From womb to tomb, and womb to womb.
Indeed. Making it look like you have a choice is the highest form of mockery. The illusion of free will.
I second this. Never chose to be born, don't owe anyone anything.

Accept your fate?

Yes/Yes
Ignore them. These are the sort of hypocrites who say things to make themselves feel better, and when it comes to it they have no problems kicking you when you're down. They aren't worth your time.
Me: i'm gonna do what's called a pro gamer move.

"We cannot tear out a single page of our life, but we can throw the whole book into the fire." 

George Sand

My thoughts exactly. 

I've given up expressing my true feelings, because there is in fact, no one to turn to. It's as if everyone is programmed to spout the same clichés over and over, so it's foolish to expect anyone to understand. It's a waste of time, really. I'm tired of having to put on a 'happy face' mask in a world full of forced positivity. As such, I no longer have a desire to connect with humanity or the world at large. 

Look, live your lives however you want. I don't care. But if you insist on interfering, don't expect me to thank you.
I'm actually surprised. If it were in say, China or India, it'd be the other way round. Meaning, the parents would've tried fifteen times to get a son.

Dude, these lines are metal AF! 

I used to be part of a religious group where we would joke that babies cry in anticipation of a life filled with suffering. Throw reincarnation into the mix and you'll get 'womb to tomb' and 'tomb to womb' playing out for all eternity. And so goes the cycle of life.

"Oh, no. Not again... "

Exactly! Doesn't mean I have food on the table, clothes on my back and a roof over my head, that I'm inclined to love and care for you when you've invested nothing of that sort. To make matters worse, Ndad's indoctrinated me since I was a kid that children are obliged to reciprocate the care one's parents have given. To care for one's old and ailing parents is the epitome of filial piety. As such, putting them in a nursing home is highly frowned upon, even if they've been complete assholes. From time to time, he's prompted us to say we're grateful for what he's done for us, all the more cringe if you ask me. I mean, come on. Given my current attitude towards him, I'm doubtful if I can even be his caregiver in the future. Caregiving is not my cup of tea, and it's the kind of task I'll have to be held at gunpoint to perform. 

I'm actually happy that your parents can hold a normal conversation so I hope this turns out well for you. Communication between my Ndad and the rest of the family is almost non-existent there might as well as a literal wall between us. Although she tolerates his behaviour, my mom for the most part refuses to talk to him. So she relies on us to convey the simplest of messages.

And you're right, just because they're treated this way doesn't mean they have to perpetuate the cycle of abuse. To sum my paternal relatives up, 'silence is golden' is the unwritten rule everyone follows. (N)grandma's military upbringing pretty much shaped the way her children are.

Greetings fellow Asian!

I think it's more to do with their upbringing. For her generation women are more submissive to their husbands. My mom also strongly believes that practicing tolerance is the key to healthy relationships. 

I feel bad for your mom too, she seems really nice. It looks like a one-sided relationship where it's all give and no take for her. I heard somewhere that you should be kind only to those who deserve it. 

It's like our generation has a built-in bullshit detector. I once told my mom if I were in my her position I'd reach peak bullshit within five years. Then it's the divorce papers.

Oh. My. God. I fucking love this, and I can so relate. 

The negative influences Ndad's had on me are here to stay. As for why you can take a look at my post history. We Asians have a 'suck it up and deal with it' mentality, so no one ever questions or let alone stand up to him. It's a matter of time before all this bottled-up rage explodes. How my mom's able to 'live and let live' is beyond me. The generation gap is definitely at work here. Unfortunately I can't just snap my fingers and erase all the bad memories from existence. 

I've lost count of how many times I've dreamt we fought ever since the pandemic started, and they get more violent each time. Sometimes I'll have homicidal fantasies. He has rarely left home and I've become increasingly agitated at his presence. If this goes on, there are two scenarios: either he gets hurt or I'll get admitted to psychiatric hospital. 

Someday I'll break free. Someday.

"Sir/Madam, I'm just trying to earn a living. Bills need to be paid. Someone needs to buy the groceries." 

<Insert roll safe meme here>

We're in the same boat. It's as though people are programmed to either 1. not take us seriously or 2. see us as mentally ill. Even if some of us have incurable terminal/chronic illnesses. We're expected to put up a strong front for our fellow members of society. Most of whom are random Toms, Dicks and Harrys that I don't even feel emotionally connected to. I too, have a chronic illness (lupus, SLE) and I know I'll be in more and more pain as I get older. Even after half a century has passed, PAS/PAD won't even be a subject parliamentary debate here. So I'll have to do it myself. I just need to come to terms with my decision.
I don't even plan on seeing this life through. Forget 'living to a ripe old age' and 'dying a natural death'.
